Professional internship/job offer missing official Business ID (CIN/GST)

recommendation.title: ⚠️ Watch for Hidden Fees
recommendation.description: Even if this letter is free, scam companies often ask for "Server/Hosting Fees" or "Security Deposits" during orientation. Never pay to work.

recommendation.title: Verify company on MCA Portal
recommendation.description: Check if the company is legally registered on the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) website. Legitimate registration does not always mean legitimate behavior.

recommendation.title: Research reviews on Glassdoor/LinkedIn
recommendation.description: Check platforms like Glassdoor, AmbitionBox, or LinkedIn for reviews from other candidates regarding "Paid" internships.

recommendation.title: Educate yourself about scams
recommendation.description: Read our comprehensive guide on identifying common fraud tactics used in India.

aiInsight: I've analyzed this internship offer from "Internboot," and while it looks professional, I noticed a significant red flag: it's missing crucial official company identifiers like a Corporate Identification Number (CIN) or Goods and Services Tax (GST) number. In India, the absence of these details makes it very difficult to verify if "Internboot" is a legally registered and legitimate business, which is a common characteristic of job scams that might later demand fees or exploit your time without proper compensation.
